evidence.title: Automation conditions affect later manual response time in a bounded experiment
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: Eighty undergraduates completed a simulated navigation task across five automation conditions. After assistance was withdrawn, final-scenario response times differed across conditions, including a significant manual-versus-fully-automated contrast. Accuracy and workload did not significantly differ; confidence did not decline as hypothesized. Observation period and measurement context: Brief simulated task exposure; experimental calendar dates not established.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; study or measurement; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition

source_locations.SRC-140: Author-uploaded article: Method and Results, printed pp. 386–389 and Figure 3; publisher metadata

evidence.limitations: Student sample, simplified task, short exposure, explicit failure and advance warning. The programmed 30-second monitoring/veto interval is not observed takeover latency. Exact plotted means were not reliably extracted. Not proof of skill decay or one unique mechanism.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: An available override does not establish immediate effective diagnosis and action.
evidence.dispute_status: See source version and dispute qualifications; no systematic clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Chaperoning
terms.definition: The continuing supervisory activity of independently observing consequential behavior, exercising informed judgment, and intervening effectively when appropriate. This requires access, competence, authority, and an actual ability to alter outcomes—not nominal participation or an agent merely stating that an action is inappropriate.

relationships.explanation: Illustrates awareness and assessment requirements alongside nominal intervention ability.
